div.l: Full big he was of braun̄ and bones
That proued wel for ouerall ther he cam
At the wrasteling he wold ay haue the Ram
He was short shuldred thikke squarre
Ther was no dore that he ne wold heue of þᵉ harre
Or breke it at arenne with his hed
His berd as any cole fox was red
And therto brode as any spade
Vpon̄ his coppe of his nose a wrette he hade
And theron̄ stood a tuft of heres
Red as the bristelis of sowes eres
His nose thrilles blake were and wide
A swerd and a bokeler bar he be his side
His mouth as gret was as a forneys
He was a iangeler and a galiardeys
And that was most of synne and harlotries
Wel coude he stele corn and tolle thries
And yit had he a thombe of gold parde
A white cote and a blew hood had he
A bag pipe wel coude he blowe ⁊and soune
And therwith all he brouȝt vs out of toune
A gentil Manciple ther was of a temple
Of wich all Catours miȝt take ensample
For to be wise in beying of vitaill
For wethir that he paid or took be taill
Alway he waited so that in his akate
That he was ay beforn and in good estate
Now is nat that of god a full gret grace
That such a leude man̄ his witt shal pace
The wisdam of an hepe of lerned men
Of maistries had he mo than thries ten̄
That were of lawe expert and curious
Of wich thei weren a dosein in that hous
Worthi to ben Stiwardes of rente and londe
Of any lord that is in Engelond
To make him lyue be his propre good
In honoure detteles but if he were wood
Or lyue statly as him list desire
And able helpen̄ all ashire
In any caas that miȝt falle or happe
And yit this Manciple sett her alder cappe
The Reue was a slendir colerik man̄
His berd was shaue as ny as euer he can̄
His heer was be his eres full round I shore
His toppe was dockid lik a preest before
Full longe were his leggis and full lene
Lik a staf ther nas no calf I sene
Wel coude he kepe a berne or a bynne
That ther nas Auditour coude of him winne
Wel wist he be the drouȝt and be the reyne
The yelding of his seed and of his grein
His lond his shepe his neet and his deiry
His swyn his hors his stoor and his pultry
Was holi in this Reues gouerning
And be his couenant yef the rekening
Sythen̄ that his lord was twenti wyntyr of age
Ther coude noman bringen him in arerage
Ther nas bailly heerde nor othir hynde
That he ne knewe his sleiȝte and his couning
They were adrad of him as of the deth
His comyng was ful faire vpon an heth
With grene shadewed was his place
He couthe better than his lord purchace
Full riche he was and stored preuily
His lorde couthe he plesen sotilly
To lene and yef him of his ougne good
And haue a thank and yit a cote and hood
In youthe he had lered a good mester
He was a full good write a Carpenter
This Reue sat vpon a full good stott
That was pomely grey and hiȝt scott
A longe furred cote of Perce he had
And be his side he bar arusti blad
Of Norfolk was this Reue of wich I telle
Beside a toun men clepe it Baldeswelle
Tukkid he was as it were a frere aboute
And euer he rod hinderest of the route
A Sompnor was there with vs in that place
That had a faire red cherubynnes face
For saucefleme he was with yhen narwe
All hoot he was and leccherous as a sparwe
With scalled browes blake and piled berde
Of his visage childre were aferd
Ther nas quik siluer litarge nor brymston
Boras Seruce ne oyle of Tartere non
No oynement that wold clensen and byte
That him miȝt helpe of whelkes white
Ne of his knobbes sitting on his chekes
Wel loued he garlik onyons and lekes
And for to drinke red wyn red as blood
